data.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
data.summary: St. Kitts and Nevis has had no personal income tax since 1980 and has no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. Capital gains are untaxed unless the asset is sold within one year of purchase (then at most 20% under the Income Tax Act). Dividends are not taxed for residents. Real estate transfers bear 6-10% seller stamp duty and a 10% alien landholding licence for non-resident buyers. Citizenship by investment from USD 250,000 (Sustainable Island State Contribution).

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: No personal income tax; no estate or wealth taxes.
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident; non-citizens need a residence permit or citizenship.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on gains from assets held more than one year. Gains on assets sold within a year of purchase are taxed at the lower of half the effective corporate rate or 20%.
capital_gains.regional_differences: Nevis has its own Island Administration and legislation for some fees and stamp duties; not researched.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on transfers of real property 6%-10% depending on consideration and location, payable by the seller; non-resident purchasers need an alien landholding licence costing the greater of 10% of value or XCD 750. Share transfers: 2% stamp duty paid by the seller.

income.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis

income_tax.summary: There is no individual income tax. Employees pay 5% social security up to XCD 6,500 a month and a graduated Housing and Social Development Levy (3.5%, 10%, 12%) on monthly earnings above XCD 2,253.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed persons between 16 and 62 pay 10% of their selected income category, subject to the contribution ceiling of XCD 6,500 a month (XCD 78,000 a year): Social Security Regulations, Schedule 1 Part III and Schedule 2 (Cap. 22.10, 2017 revision). The Housing and Social Development Levy does not apply to self-employment income: the Act imposes it on 'the wages of every person employed' (s.3) and defines 'employed person' by reference to the employments in the First Schedule to the Social Security Act (s.2); no provision charges self-employed persons. Employer-side items (5% + 1% injury + 3% levy + 1% severance) are not counted.
income_tax.local_tax_note: KNA has no personal income tax (Deloitte). The wage brackets are the employee-paid Housing and Social Development Levy, a levy on employees' wages (Cap. 20.21, s.3), expressed annually from Deloitte's monthly bands (XCD 2,253.33 / 6,500 / 8,000 times 12): nil up to XCD 27,040; 3.5% on earnings to XCD 78,000; 10% to XCD 96,000; 12% above. The statute's 2017 text shows a lower nil band (XCD 18,720); Deloitte's 2026 figure is used. It is kept in the brackets because it is a levy on employment income and the only direct charge on pay, but it is a payroll levy, not an income tax, and it does not apply to self-employed income, so a self-employed nomad pays social security only. The Inland Revenue Department now refers to a 'Social Services Levy' on wages (December 2025 bonus waiver notice); whether this is the renamed levy was not confirmed. It is charged on top of the 5% social security contribution (capped at XCD 78,000). The self-employed brackets are nil, because the levy does not reach self-employment income.

succession.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
succession.summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis has no forced heirship in the sources read. Nevis offers international trusts that foreign heirship rules cannot attack, and a Multiform Foundation. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states the federation's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
succession.trust_note: Not in the HCCH status table. The Nevis regulator says an international trust cannot be declared void because of forced heirship rules of the settlor's domicile. Foundations: Nevis Multiform Foundations Ordinance, Cap. 7.08(N) (Ordinance 2 of 2004, amended 2011), with the same protection. IFC Review also lists St Kitts as having foundation legislation (not named).
open_questions: Succession law on St Kitts and Nevis themselves (wills, family provision) was not read.
Name of the Nevis trust ordinance and any St Kitts foundation act not confirmed.

immigration.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
immigration.summary: EU, US and other passport holders all need a permit or citizenship to live here; there is no free movement. The cheapest way to a passport is the Sustainable Island State Contribution from USD 250,000 (or USD 250,000 to a public benefit project; real estate from USD 325,000). Ordinary residence routes (homeowner, self-sufficient temporary residence) exist but could only be sourced from secondary guides.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation under the Citizenship Act is reported at 14 years of residence immediately before the application (government service can shorten it); good character required. Not read in full from the statute.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: The Citizenship Unit states that dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens.

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Sustainable Island State Contribution (SISC)
routes.summary: A non-refundable contribution of USD 250,000 to the national fund gives citizenship with no residence requirement.
routes.requirements: Minimum USD 250,000 for the main applicant (earlier note: includes family of up to four, with USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18 and USD 50,000 per extra dependant 18+; not re-verified this pass). Applicant must be 18+, pass due diligence and meet financial criteria. Disqualified if refused citizenship or a visa by any visa-free partner country (unless since obtained), criminal record or active investigation, or bankruptcy within 10 years. Applications from Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea and Russia are not accepted; nationality exclusions apply within the OTHER group. Applications go through an authorised agent.
routes.investment_options: SISC USD 250,000; Public Benefit Option USD 250,000 (approved projects); Developer real estate USD 325,000; private real estate USD 600,000.
routes.fees_note: Due diligence and processing fees not re-verified on the Citizenship Unit pages reached this pass (earlier note: USD 10,000 main applicant, USD 7,500 per dependant 16+). See open questions.
routes.physical_presence: None. The Citizenship Unit states there is no residency requirement.
routes.family: Spouse, children under 18 (to 30 if in full-time study and supported), disabled adult children, and parents 55+ supported by and living with the applicant.
routes.tax_note: No personal income tax in St Kitts and Nevis, but CBI citizens must file a final return and obtain a clearance certificate on emigrating (earlier Deloitte note). Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere.
